description: A complete, deterministic chain scenario — genesis, an appended block, a foreign-reference block by a second author, a meta-molecule published with the meta-bond it uses, and a rotation with its successor genesis — plus a fork, the blocks a conforming implementation MUST reject on their bytes, and the blocks it MUST reject only once it holds the chains around them. Ed25519 signing is deterministic, so every signature here is reproducible from the seeds in inputs.

inputs.note: Every key comes from a seed of 32 equal bytes. These are test keys with published private material and MUST NOT be used for anything but conformance testing. public_key_text is the canonical text form of public_key — multibase base32 over 0xed 0x01 || key (spec/03-encoding.md, "Text representation of author keys") — and an implementation MUST reproduce it from the key bytes.

sections.name: chain
sections.description: The scenario, in the order the blocks are published. A consumer that stores them in order and validates each one MUST accept all six; the digests link them, so any encoding difference shows up as a broken prev.

cases.name: alice_genesis
cases.description: Alice's genesis block: prev is null, and the four operations define two atoms, a bond and the molecule that uses them. The molecule's references resolve inside this same block.
cases.author: alice

cases.name: alice_second
cases.description: The next block of Alice's chain: prev is the digest of alice_genesis. Its molecule carries a scalar filler with a unit, whose digest is the metre atom this block defines.
cases.author: alice

cases.name: bob_foreign_reference
cases.description: Bob's genesis block, referencing Alice's genesis block in refs. Its molecule uses a bond and an atom defined there and an atom defined by its own first operation.
cases.author: bob

cases.name: bob_meta_molecule
cases.description: The next block of Bob's chain: a meta-molecule asserting the molecule bob_foreign_reference published, together with the create_bond that publishes the standard meta-bond "_A_ is true" it is built from. A meta-bond is an entity like any other and is present in no chain until an author creates it, so this is the shape a publishable truth assertion has; drop the create_bond and the block is the invalid_in_chain case unreachable_meta_bond. refs is empty: the asserted molecule was created by an ancestor of this block's own chain.
cases.author: bob

cases.name: alice_rotation
cases.description: The rotation block that ends Alice's chain. Exactly one rotate_key operation, prev not null, and new_pub naming a different key.
cases.author: alice

cases.name: alice_successor_genesis
cases.description: The successor chain's genesis block. It is public and names the rotation block in refs, which is what makes the succession verifiable to a node with no keys.
cases.author: alice_successor

sections.name: forks
sections.description: Two blocks of one chain sharing a prev. Detection is normative; what a node does about it is not.

cases.name: alice_second_vs_alice_fork
cases.description: Two blocks signed by Alice carry the same prev. A node that holds both MUST detect the fork; whether it rejects, flags or keeps the first is its own policy.
cases.author: alice

sections.name: fork_block
sections.description: The forking block in full. It is a well-formed, correctly signed block: what makes it a fork is the chain it arrives into, not anything inside it.

cases.name: alice_fork
cases.description: A second block claiming alice_genesis as its predecessor. It is valid in isolation; against a store that already holds alice_second it is a fork.
cases.author: alice

sections.name: invalid
sections.description: Blocks a conforming implementation MUST reject, each naming the rule it violates. Every one of them is canonical dCBOR and — except where the case is about the signature — correctly signed, so the rejection can only come from the named rule.

cases.name: tampered_signature
cases.reason: A valid genesis block with one bit of its sig field flipped.

cases.name: unknown_version
cases.reason: The v field is 2. A field a later version introduces arrives in a block this version rejects on its version, never as an extra key.

cases.name: unknown_block_type
cases.reason: The type field is "secret". There are exactly three block types.

cases.name: empty_ops
cases.reason: The ops list is empty.

cases.name: unknown_block_key
cases.rule: spec/02-block-format.md, Validation rule 8 (deterministic encoding, including the closed-map rule)
cases.reason: The block map carries a "note" key its definition does not declare. An unknown key is a rejection, never something to ignore: a decoder that ignored it would hash bytes it did not account for.

cases.name: missing_block_key
cases.rule: spec/02-block-format.md, Validation rule 8 (deterministic encoding, including the closed-map rule)
cases.reason: The block map omits the declared ts key.

cases.name: public_block_with_enc
cases.reason: A public block carrying an enc field, which belongs to a private block.

cases.name: unknown_operation
cases.rule: spec/02-block-format.md, Validation rule 8 (deterministic encoding, including the closed-map rule)
cases.reason: An operation whose op value is "delete_atom". There are exactly four operation types.

cases.name: unknown_operation_key
cases.rule: spec/02-block-format.md, Validation rule 8 (deterministic encoding, including the closed-map rule)
cases.reason: A create_atom operation carrying an extra "lang" key. The closed-map rule governs operation maps too.

cases.name: rotate_key_in_public_block
cases.reason: A rotate_key operation in a public block. It may appear only in a rotation block, so that a chain ends where the type field says it ends.

cases.name: rotation_block_as_genesis
cases.reason: A rotation block with a null prev. A rotation block ends a chain, and there is no chain to end.

cases.name: rotation_block_two_operations
cases.reason: A rotation block carrying a second operation. It MUST contain exactly one rotate_key operation and no others.

cases.name: rotation_to_the_same_key
cases.reason: new_pub equals the block's own pub. A chain would end in favour of itself.

cases.name: duplicate_refs
cases.reason: The refs list names the same digest twice. The duplicate half of rule 10 is structural and is checked at decoding.

cases.name: cid_in_prev
cases.reason: The prev field carries a 36-byte CIDv1 instead of the raw 32-byte digest. Internal references are digests; the CID appears only at the API boundary.

cases.name: filler_type_out_of_range
cases.reason: A filler of type 5. The v1 vocabulary is types 0 to 4.

cases.name: filler_value_shape_mismatch
cases.reason: A type 0 filler carrying text. Each type tag is bound to exactly one value shape.

cases.name: empty_fillers
cases.reason: A create_molecule operation with an empty fillers list; the CDDL requires at least one.

cases.name: private_block_with_plaintext_ops
cases.reason: A private block carrying a plaintext ops field. Its operations live inside enc.

cases.name: private_block_short_enc
cases.reason: An enc field shorter than the 16-byte Poly1305 tag cannot be the output of the AEAD.

cases.name: private_block_wrong_nonce_size
cases.reason: A 12-byte nonce. XChaCha20 takes 24 bytes.

cases.name: private_block_missing_nonce
cases.rule: spec/02-block-format.md, Validation rule 8 (deterministic encoding, including the closed-map rule)
cases.reason: A private block with no nonce field.

cases.name: signed_by_another_key
cases.reason: A block claiming Alice's pub and signed by Bob's key.

sections.name: invalid_in_chain
sections.description: Blocks that decode, verify and are wrong only in relation to what a node holds: rules 3, 4, 5, 6, the own-chain half of rule 10, and the scan limit. Replay each case's setup blocks into a fresh store, in order, accepting every one of them, then offer bytes: it MUST be rejected under the named rule. A case carrying scan_limit MUST be validated with that limit configured, and is valid under the default.

cases.name: prev_of_another_chain
cases.reason: The rejected block is signed by Bob and its prev names a block of Alice's chain. Within a single chain all blocks MUST carry the same pub, so this is not a link but a claim on someone else's history. The block decodes and its signature verifies; only the store can refuse it.

cases.name: appended_after_rotation
cases.reason: The rejected block is appended by Alice's key to the rotation block that ended her chain. The rotation block marks the key inactive: implementations MUST NOT accept a further block signed by it, whatever that block contains (spec/02-block-format.md, "rotate_key").

cases.name: refs_names_own_chain
cases.reason: The rejected block lists its own predecessor in refs. Every block of a chain carries the same pub, so the check is a comparison of the referenced block's pub with the referencing block's; it needs the referenced block, which is why the duplicate half of rule 10 is a decoder's business and this half is not.

cases.name: unreachable_bond
cases.reason: The create_molecule names a bond that no block defines: not this one, not an ancestor — it is a genesis block — and not through refs, which is empty. The store holds another author's block, and holding blocks is not reachability.

cases.name: bond_defined_in_an_unreferenced_chain
cases.reason: The bond exists and the node holds the block that created it, but the rejected block's refs is empty. Reachability is a property of the block, not of the node's store: prev is not a resolution path into another author's chain, and an entity a node happens to know is not a dependency the block declared.

cases.name: unreachable_meta_bond
cases.reason: The create_molecule names the standard meta-bond "_A_ is true", which nothing in this chain ever created: the block publishes no create_bond for it, its ancestor published the molecule being asserted and not the meta-bond, and refs is empty. The standard meta-bonds are not implicitly present in any chain and no digest is exempt from rule 4 (spec/06-meta-bonds.md, "Meta-molecules are regular molecules"), so an implementation that recognizes the five meta-bond digests and lets them resolve accepts this block. Its valid counterpart is the chain block bob_meta_molecule, which is this block plus the create_bond.

cases.name: forward_reference_in_same_block
cases.reason: The create_molecule comes first and the operations that define its bond and its fillers come after it. Operations are ordered and the order is the evaluation order: an operation may reference what an earlier operation created, never what a later one will. Setup is empty — the store cannot help a block that is wrong about itself.

cases.name: unreachable_scalar_unit
cases.reason: Every digest in the block resolves except the unit inside a scalar filler, whose atom is defined in a chain the block does not reference. The unit is an internal reference like any other and rule 4 covers it: "There is no exempt position — every digest an operation carries is subject to this rule."

cases.name: scan_limit_exceeded
cases.rule: spec/05-processing-model.md, Scan limit (rejected under Validation rule 4)
cases.reason: The bond resolves three foreign blocks deep: the rejected block names Alice's block, which names Dave's, which names Carol's, where the bond was created. Validate it with the scan_limit of this case, 2, and resolution must stop before the third block and treat the block as invalid for unresolvable references. Under the default limit of 256 the same block against the same store is valid — that is what the case isolates. One unit is one distinct foreign block scanned, so an implementation counting digests or recursion levels will disagree here.

cases.name: bond_resolves_to_an_atom
cases.reason: The create_molecule's bond field names a digest that resolves — through refs, to Alice's block — to an atom. Reachability alone is satisfied, which is why this is rule 5 and not rule 4: the data model binds each position to a kind, and a molecule built on an atom is not a statement.

cases.name: unit_resolves_to_a_bond
cases.reason: The unit inside a scalar filler resolves, through refs, to a bond. A unit MUST resolve to an atom: it names what the number is measured in. The digest is reachable, so an implementation that checks rule 4 on the unit position and stops there accepts this block.

cases.name: filler_count_mismatch
cases.reason: The molecule carries one filler and its bond's template, defined in the block Alice published and this block references, has two variables. The count cannot be checked without resolving the bond, which is why a decoder accepts these bytes and a node does not.

cases.name: public_block_references_a_private_block
cases.reason: The rejected block is public and its refs name a private block of Alice's chain. Nothing about the bytes says so — the type is inside the referenced block — so the rejection arrives only once the node holds it. The setup's private block carries a fixed opaque ciphertext: no node without the key reads it, which is precisely the reason for the rule.
